label: First copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1) in long sequences whose 2nd/3rd original tokens are f/0/b/z/e/h
predicate: (recall_idx == 1) & (L >= 7) & (isin(orig(1), [tok("f"), 26, tok("b"), tok("z"), tok("e"), tok("h")]) | isin(orig(2), [tok("f"), 26, tok("b"), tok("z"), tok("e"), tok("h")]))
explanation: Fires only at one position: step L+1 (recall_idx == 1), where the input is the first original token fed back and the model has to output original token 1. Almost all activation mass (99.9%) is at that step and none appears in the original or delimiter phases. It fires on only about 12% of those steps. Which ones depends on (a) sequence length: the rate rises steeply with L (t=10/L=9 holds 44% of mass, nothing for L=3), and (b) the identity of the token being output and the one after it (orig(1), orig(2)): f is by far the strongest (24% of mass), then 0, b, z, e, h. The top activations have f in both orig(1) and orig(2) (e.g. g f f d x ...). The input token (orig(0)) has little effect. Magnitude increases with L and with how many of the early outputs are f/0. It does not fire on recall_idx 0 (the <DEL> step) or on later copy steps. The predicate catches most of the mass (~0.82 on dev) but precision is only about 0.5, so the gating on token identity looks graded rather than a clean set.
